_doc: Townsfolk courtship (systems/romance.js): who notices whom, the stages a courtship passes through, how it fails, and the words people say. Steps run every stepDays for every town with a roster; the wedding itself is the townsfolk wedding (Townsfolk._wed). Lines: a plain string, or { t, p: [tempers], s: 'high'|'low' } — a line with p/s is preferred for a speaker who matches. Tokens: {name} the other person's first name, {A}/{B} people as the town calls them, {when}, {days}, {to}, {player}.

onMap._wedding: A wedding with a church in town: the couple, their guests and the priest gather at the church door (weddingGather seconds), go in for the service (weddingService seconds: the couple before the altar, the guests in the pews, the priest's prayers and the vows, ui/innerMapCourting.js + world/innerMap/townScenes.js), then come out to the door to cheers (weddingSeconds).

flirt: Oh! {name}. I didn't see you there.
You've done something different with your hair, {name}.
Will you be at the well later, {name}?

flirt.t: Ha! {name}, you'll be the death of me.
I saved you the best of the bread, {name}. Don't tell anyone.
Walk with me a while, {name}? I'll not bite.
Tell me something I don't know, {name}.
My lady {name}. You grace the street this morning.
You've a fine eye for a horse, {name}. And for other things, I hear.

flirtReply: Maybe I will be. Maybe not.

flirtReply.t: Hmph. Flattery won't fill a basket. ...Say it again, though.

sweet: I thought of you all day, {name}.
Look, the first star. Make a wish, {name}.
I'd walk to the edge of the world with you, {name}. Or to the mill, at least.

sweet.t: When the harvest's in, I'll speak to your father, {name}.
When the harvest's in, I'll ask you properly, {name}. Before the whole town.
I wrote you a verse. It's dreadful. Don't laugh, {name}.
I'll build us a house by the river, {name}. With a proper roof.
Our families' lands lie side by side, {name}. Fate, I'd call it.

sweetReply.t: *laughs softly* You're a fool. My fool.

gift: Flowers from the market, {name}. For you.
I brought you a ribbon, {name}. Blue, like you said.

gift.t: A little carving. It's meant to be a swan, {name}.
Silk, {name}, from the south. Nothing less would do.

giftReply: You shouldn't have. ...I'm glad you did.
*holds it close* I'll keep it always.

giftReply.t: It's a duck. But I love it.

quarrel: You were dancing with them at the fair, {name}. Don't deny it.
Always tomorrow with you, {name}. Always tomorrow!

quarrel.t: My mother says I could do better, {name}. Maybe she's right.

quarrel: Folk say I could do better, {name}. Maybe they're right.

quarrel.t: Fine! Go, then! See if I care!
*won't meet their eye* ...I'm not cross. I'm not.

quarrelReply: That's not fair and you know it.
*sighs* Can we not do this here?

quarrelReply.t: I'm sorry. I'm sorry, all right?

mope.t: Who needs them? Not me. Pass the ale.

weddingGuest: Long life to the happy couple!
Don't they make a fine pair!
To the church, to the church!
weddingCouple: Hold my hand, {name}. Don't let go.

flirting: Have you seen how {A} goes red whenever {B} walks past?
{A} has been finding reasons to stand about near {B}. Every day. Funny, that.
courting: {A} and {B} have been walking out of an evening. Everyone's seen them.
{A} is courting {B}, and making no secret of it.
{A} brought {B} flowers from the market. Flowers! The whole street talked of it.
love: {A} and {B}? Head over heels, the pair of them.
Mark my words, {A} and {B} will be wed before the year's out.
You'd think {A} and {B} invented love, the way they carry on.
betrothed: The banns are read for {A} and {B}: they wed {when}.
forbidden: {A} and {B} meet in secret, they say. Their families won't have it.
{A}'s people have forbidden the match with {B}. As if that ever stopped anyone.
rival: {A} and {C} both have their eye on {B}. It'll end in tears, or in a fight.
{C} has started calling on {B} too, and {A} is fit to burst.
quarrel: {A} and {B} had words in the street. A lovers' quarrel, nothing more.
{A} and {B} were shouting at each other by the well. They'll make it up.
playerRival: {A} was courting {B}, until {player} came to town. {A} isn't pleased.

noticing: Me? Sweet on someone? *glances toward {name}'s door* ...No.
There's no one. Well. There might be someone.
flirting: *blushes* Is it so plain? {name} has the loveliest laugh.
{name} and I... it's nothing. We talk. That's all. For now.

courting.t: {name} and I have been walking out. Don't tell my mother. ...She knows.

courting: {name} and I have been walking out. The whole street knows, I expect.
I'm courting {name}, if you must know. And I don't care who knows it.
love: I love {name}. There, I've said it out loud.
{name} is the best thing that's ever happened to me.
betrothed: {name} and I are to be wed {when}! You'll come, won't you?
We're promised, {name} and I. {when}, at the church.
forbidden: My family won't hear of {name}. They'll come round. They must.
They've forbidden me to see {name}. *lowers voice* I see them anyway.
broken: Don't speak to me of love. Not now.
{name} and I are finished. I'd rather not talk of it.
It still hurts. It'll pass, they tell me.

gossipNone: Courting? Not that I've seen. It's a quiet town for that.
No one's sweet on anyone just now. More's the pity.
tokenGive: Would you? Then give {name} this, and tell them... no, just give them this.
*presses a folded letter into your hand* For {name}. Don't read it!
tokenDeliver: From {name}? *reads, and goes quite pink* Oh. Oh my.
*holds the letter to their heart* Tell {name}... tell them yes.
goodWord: {name} said that? About me? *tries not to smile*
goodWordFail: {name} can speak for themselves, thank you.
*frowns* Did {name} send you to say that?
meddle: {name}? With someone else? *goes white* I don't believe you. ...Do I?
*quietly* I wondered. I did wonder about {name}.
meddleCaught: {name}? Never. I'll ask {name} myself, and if it's a lie you'll answer for it. *storms off to find them*
Why would you say such a thing about {name}? What are you to us?
playerRival: I know what you're about with {name}. Keep away.
You think a fine traveller turns {name}'s head? We'll see.

annals.betrothed: {A} and {B} were promised to each other {when}.
annals.jilted: {A} broke off the promise to {B} {when}. Poor {b}.
annals.eloped: {A} and {B} ran off together {when}, to {to}. Their families are beside themselves.
annals.affair: {A} was found out with {B} {when}. The whole town talks of nothing else.
